note: Read-only candidate contract for Figma. This is reference data for the runtime owner, not a profile: no credential appears here, nothing is installed, and no packaged recipe exists. Every value is synthetic.

api_version.documented: No API version or date header appears on the REST documentation, and the version is carried in the path as /v1. The only documented response headers are the rate-limit set.
api_version.note: Figma needs no static version header. That is a separate requirement from the credential-derived token header below, and the two must not be conflated.

credential_derived_required_for_personal.X-Figma-Token: <personal access token from the user keyring>
credential_derived_required_for_personal.documented: You can do so by passing the token to the API in the X-Figma-Token header of your request.

oauth_alternative.Authorization: Bearer <OAuth access token from the user keyring>
oauth_alternative.documented: When you call the API, pass a Bearer authorization header.
oauth_alternative.note: This route is compatible with the transport that exists today, but it also needs native OAuth sign-in, so it is not a shortcut around the token header.

token_endpoint_only.documented: Basic authentication is documented for POST https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/token only, not for resource calls.
token_endpoint_only.note: Recorded so the token exchange is not mistaken for a resource-call scheme.

tier.documented: This is a Tier 3 endpoint and requires the current_user:read scope.
tier.documented_meaning: Tiers are rate-limit tiers, not plan gates. Tier 3, which includes the users endpoints, is documented at up to 10 requests per minute for View and Collab seats, and at higher limits for Dev and Full seats depending on plan.
tier.correction: An earlier assessment treated Tier 3 as a paid-plan requirement. The official rate-limit documentation defines tiers by seat type and plan limits, not as a plan gate.

documented_response_fields.id: String, documented as the unique stable id of the user.
documented_response_fields.handle: String, documented as the name of the user.
documented_response_fields.img_url: String, documented as the URL link to the user's profile image.
documented_response_fields.email: String, documented as present only on the /v1/me endpoint.

limitations: No field nullability is documented, so the label is treated as required by documentation of the field's presence only.
The page frames the endpoint around OAuth 2. Whether a personal access token may call /v1/me is not documented, so a personal-token profile must prove identity before it relies on it.
email is documented as conditionally present, so it is never used as the account label; handle is.

smallest_useful_read.documented: Returns the metadata for the file referred to by :key. The file key can be parsed from any Figma file url of the form https://www.figma.com/:file_type/:file_key/:file_name.
smallest_useful_read.why_this_endpoint: Projecting a few metadata pointers does not make GET /v1/files/:key a small response. That endpoint documents the document node tree as a non-optional field of its return value, so the whole tree crosses the network before any projection happens. GET file metadata is the documented endpoint whose return value contains no document tree, which is why it, not the projection, is the smallest useful read here.

projected_fields.documented: String in the documented file metadata object.

projected_fields.documented: String in the documented file metadata object.

deliberately_not_projected.reason: Nested user objects and a signed thumbnail URL add payload and a short-lived value without helping a first metadata read, and no nullability is documented for any of them.

smallest_useful_read.documented_rate_limits: GET file metadata is documented as a Tier 3 endpoint. Tier 3 limits are documented at up to 10 per minute for View and Collab seats and at higher per-minute limits for Dev and Full seats by plan, and the documentation warns that View seat limits can be lower in practice.
smallest_useful_read.documentation_inconsistency: The rate-limit prose refers to GET file metadata as a Tier 2 endpoint limited to about six requests per month, while the tier table and the endpoint page both place it in Tier 3. Which statement governs is unverified.

document_tree_read.documented: The name, lastModified, thumbnailUrl, editorType, linkAccess and version attributes are all metadata of the retrieved file, and the document attribute contains a Node of type DOCUMENT, which the documented schema marks as a non-optional field.

traversal_parameters.ids: Documented: a comma separated list of nodes to return, and for historical reasons top-level canvas nodes are always returned regardless. The response also notes a quirk that may be removed in a future version.
traversal_parameters.depth: Documented: a positive integer for how deep into the document tree to traverse, where 1 returns only Pages and 2 returns Pages and all top level objects. Not setting it returns all nodes, and whether 0 is valid is not documented.
traversal_parameters.version: Documented: a specific version ID, defaulting to the current version when omitted.
traversal_parameters.geometry: Documented as paths to export vector data.
traversal_parameters.plugin_data: Documented as a comma separated list of plugin IDs or shared.

transport_bound.engine_fact: Steed's recipe transport reads a response body in bounded chunks and fails the request with an API error once the body exceeds 128 KiB, in services/recipe_http.py.
transport_bound.consequence: A file read therefore succeeds or fails on the size of the whole response, before any projection. Selecting five metadata pointers does not reduce what crosses the network.
transport_bound.documented_provider_fact: Figma publishes no response-size limit or size guidance for any file endpoint. The only size statement on the file endpoint page is about rendered images, up to 32 megapixels.
transport_bound.pending: Whether a real design file of ordinary size fits inside the transport bound cannot be answered from documentation on either side, and is not claimed either way.

requirements_for_any_document_read: A reviewed fixed query input for depth or ids, because the transport today accepts only the reviewed pagination parameter.
Acceptance that a bounded document read is useful at all, given the documented rate limits.

binary_content.documented: GET /v1/images/:key returns a map from node ids to URLs of rendered images, warns that a map value may be null when rendering failed, and documents that the image assets will expire after 30 days. GET /v1/files/:key/images returns URLs that expire in no more than 14 days.
binary_content.note: No endpoint returns image bytes, so serving design or image content stays a separate workspace capability.

read_contract.paging: The file endpoints are not documented as paged.

documented_statuses.403: The request was valid but the server refuses action, including when the caller lacks permissions or uses HTTP instead of HTTPS. The file endpoint documents 403 for an invalid or expired developer or OAuth token.
documented_statuses.404: The requested file or resource was not found. The file endpoint documents 404 when the specified file was not found.
documented_statuses.429: Requests may be throttled or rate limited; the documentation asks the client to wait and retries, typically after a minute.

failure_contract.no_401_documented: The errors documentation does not list 401, so a profile must not rely on 401 for an invalid token.

failure_document.documented_message: The developer / OAuth token is invalid or expired.
failure_document.note: No global JSON error envelope is documented for Figma. The err property appears only as a response field on the images endpoint. A framework test should assert status handling only and must not depend on an undocumented error body.

rate_limit_headers.Retry-After: Integer, how long before retrying, in seconds.

framework_gap.minimum_missing_behavior: Carry a user credential in a service-specific token header such as X-Figma-Token, without pretending it is a Bearer token and without putting it in a path or query. That alone keeps the metadata endpoint out of reach today.
not_required_for_a_first_read: Any version or date header, since Figma documents none and carries the version in the path.
OAuth sign-in, if a personal access token may call the identity and file metadata endpoints, which only a real account can settle.
A fixed depth query input, because GET file metadata returns no document tree.
List paging, which the file endpoints do not document.
required_for_a_document_read: A reviewed fixed query input for depth or ids, which is listed as its own capability.
An empirical answer on whether a real file response fits the transport bound.
framework_gap.not_a_gap: Nothing here requires weakening origin rules, adding a credential to a path, or bypassing a documented restriction.

empirical_status.policy: Documentation proves what an endpoint offers. A framework test can only prove Steed's own behaviour against a documented shape. Neither can show that a provider accepts a credential or sends a field, so those stay pending until a real account is used.
settled_by_documentation: GET file metadata exists, needs file_metadata:read, is documented as Tier 3, and its return value contains no document tree.
GET /v1/files/:key documents the document tree as a non-optional field and documents depth and ids as the only traversal limits.
No response-size limit is documented for any file endpoint.
Tier 3 limits are documented per seat type and plan, with a stated View seat caveat.
